provenance: All content written for this project; not consulted against R-010 (מאל"ו), R-013 (AnkiWeb), or any NC-licensed dictionary.
source: data/amirnet-vocab.csv (Tier 1, A2) — K-005, alphabetical continuation from "medal" (the endpoint of the previous batch, batch-2026-09-14-3.jsonl, verified live against the CSV and every existing batch-*.jsonl headword before writing), through "orphan". "Olympic" (the alphabetical entry between "occupation" and "onion") was skipped: it is a proper adjective derived from a proper noun (the Olympic Games), the same class of headword NGSL-era batches have always excluded (lesson 1, §A1) even though this queue is CEFR-J rather than NGSL — flagged here rather than written silently.
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a scratch script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not pushed) against the full draft set, then re-verified via parseBatchFile on the final .jsonl file through npm run measure:gate — 17/17 pass, 0 rejected. A one-row negative control (Latin letters in translation_he, single-letter out-of-level item stems) was run first through the same checker and correctly rejected on both axes, confirming the checker script itself is wired to the real gate. Every non-headword content word in every example and stem was checked against data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt with grep -x before a single sentence was finalised (§A1 rule 4); six first-draft rejections (level drift on "struck"/"twelve", "friday", "two", "classroom", "pan", plus one distractor colliding with the headword's own inflection set and one distractor accidentally repeating the headword) were caught by that pre-check plus one round of the real gate and fixed before the file was written — see the lesson entry in plan/80-content-lessons.md.
batch_size_note: 17 rows. Sized to what this tick's window could draft with full sentences/items/distractors (T-353, which would make sentence-less rows legal and let a tick cover many more headwords, is still ⬜ — see the tick's report to Roy), gate for real, and verify end to end, well under the 1,200-row-per-file ceiling in lib/core/spotCheck.ts. Not derived from any per-batch quota — CONTENT.md states there is none.
pos_correction_note: "million" carries pos=number in data/amirnet-vocab.csv, which is not one of the nine POS_VALUES gateSense accepts. Following the precedent set for "hundred"/"thousand" (lesson 46, C-0586): written here as pos=determiner, is_function_word:true.
he_one_to_many_note: "noon" and "midday" share the same natural Hebrew translation (צהריים) — tagged he_one_to_many_group on both rows rather than inventing two artificially distinct Hebrew words for one shared meaning.
next_marker: orphan → next alphabetical Tier 1 single-word headword after this batch (checked live against data/amirnet-vocab.csv and all batch-*.jsonl files as of this tick, skipping the same categories earlier batches skipped — inflections already covered under their base form, hyphenated/multi-word compounds, abbreviations, and now also "Olympic" as a proper adjective) is "oven".
